name: FlowContainer
description: The theming bridge for a React Flow canvas: a Box around `<ReactFlow>` that declares xyflow's `--xy-*` variables from the palette in both themes, so the canvas names no colour and its dark mode belongs to the page. It imports nothing from xyflow — pass `colorMode={flowColorMode(theme)}` to `<ReactFlow>` so its own `.dark` class agrees.

props.name: tokens
props.description: The canvas's roles — `surface`, `panel`, `text`, `border`, `grid`, `edge`, `selection`, `handle` — each a token for both themes (`{ selection: 'sky-500' }`) or one per theme (`{ surface: { light: 'base-50', dark: 'base-950' } }`). One `--xy-*` variable is plain `vars`, because the container is a Box.

props.name: motion
props.description: `'static'` zeroes every Box transition inside the canvas, layers' entrances included — for a canvas whose nodes are Boxes moved or resized every frame, which the default `transition: all` would make trail the pointer.

a11y: A `<div>` with variables on it: no role, no name. React Flow owns the canvas's accessibility; a custom node or edge gets a visible focus from `flowNodeStyles`/`flowEdgeStyles`.
